the whole suite\n --exclude-skills Run the 'without skills' arm: no skills are pinned, and the run is la
belled as excluded\n --refresh-snapshot PERSISTS a new host-config snapshot on the suite, changing every f
uture run of it. Single-target runs only.\n --notes <text> Free-text note stored on the run\n --min-p
ass-rate <n> Pass threshold for this run (0-100)\n --match-options <json> Tool-call matc
h options for this run, e.g. '{\"toolCallOrder\":\"exact\"}'\n --idempotency-key <key> Retry key for a lost lau
nch response; for --file, one is minted and printed when omitted\n --wait Wait for every start
ed run to reach a terminal status\n --wait-timeout <ms> Maximum time to wait for completion (default 600000
; a run held for its judge gets up to 31 more minutes unless this flag is set)\n --reporter <json-summary|junit-xml|html> Render
the completed run report to stdout\n --out <path> Atomically write the completed report selected by
--reporter (default: json-summary)\n --compose-client <id-or-name> Compose a stack to run instead of naming a saved
environment: the client it runs as. Default is EPHEMERAL (does not attach to the suite).\n --compose-host <id-or-name>
Deprecated alias for --compose-client\n --compose-computer <id-or-name> Sandbox image to pin on the composed stack\
n --compose-model <id...> Model(s) to run on the composed stack. Replaces the client default unless --with-clie
nt-default is set.\n --compose-model-selection <json...> A whole saved model selection (source, connection, settings.reason
ingEffort) as JSON (or @file, or -): one cell for its model, at its effort. Alongside --compose-model. Repeat it to add several se
lections for one model (e.g. at low and at high) — each distinct selection is its own cell.\n --with-client-default
Also launch an inherit cell that uses each client's pinned model, alongside --compose-model\n --save-targets
Attach the composed environments to the suite (append, capped at 10). Default is ephemeral.\n --compose-server <id-
or-name...> Server(s) to pin on the composed stack. Snapshots them into a server group, so the run keeps testing these se
rvers even if the host's own server list changes later. Mutually exclusive with --compose-server-group.\n --compose-server-group
<id> Standalone server group to pin on the composed stack\n --compose-host-servers No longer sup
ported: eval runs take their servers from a server group. Use --compose-server or --compose-server-group.\n --compose-skill <id..
.> Project-shared skill IDs to pin on the composed stack\n --compose-secret <id...> Project SE
CRET IDs the composed stack grants to its runs. Without one a composed stack carries no credential — list them with `mcpjam secret
s list`.\n --allow-approximated <case...> Approve an `approximated` imported case for THIS RUN ONLY (authored case id)
. Repeatable. --file only, and requires --approval-reason.\n --approval-reason <text> Why the approximations nam
ed by --allow-approximated are acceptable for this run (1-500 characters). Recorded on the run by the server.\n -h, --help

cases for your MCP server, run them across models, and gate pass/fail on deterministic assertions plus optional LLM-as-judge.\n23:
A group of cases plus the defaults they share: attached servers, models to run against, default assertions, judge config, and argu
ment-matching mode.\n27:One scenario you want to verify — a prompt (or a sequence of prompts), the tools you expect to fire, an op
tional expected output, and the assertions that decide pass/fail.\n43:Every case opens in the spine, however it was authored — in
the app, through the CLI, or from an SDK suite file. The spine is a flat, ordered list of steps. Each step is one of:\n45:* **Prom
pt** — a user turn the model receives. The first prompt is always present; use **Add assertion or action** to add a second prompt
for multi-turn cases.\n47:* **Assert** — an assertion that grades the case.\n53:Use **Add assertion or action** to add an assertio
n, a second prompt, or an interact step. Each assertion row says what it checks, who wrote it, and what a miss does:\n56:* **Step
N** — an assertion written as a step (what the CLI and the SDK produce). It is graded in place, at its position in the run, and is
labelled by that position: a step-level \"no tool errors\" reads **No tool errors so far**, because it only sees the transcript u
p to that point. Editing one rewrites that step; it never becomes a case-level assertion.\n57:* **This case** — an assertion you a
dded here. It is graded once, over the finished transcript.\n60:The list reads as a checklist with progressive disclosure. An off
row shows only its short name. Once on, clicking the name opens an inline editor showing the full criterion, the **Required / Advi
sory** role control, and any editable fields (thresholds, match criteria). Multiple editors can stay open at once. An assertion th
at carries a number (such as a latency budget) shows it under the name at rest.\n62:A row's **role** says what a miss does: **Requ
ired** fails the trial, **Advisory** shows the miss without failing it. The control appears when your deployment supports assertio
